question: What does the neural tangent kernel framework rigorously explain about neural-network training, generalization, finite-width behavior, and applications, and where does its fixed-feature infinite-width approximation fail?

key_findings.claim: In the infinite-width NTK parameterization, gradient descent becomes kernel gradient flow with an initialization-determined kernel that stays constant.
key_findings.evidence: The survey derives the empirical parameter-gradient kernel, its square-loss closed-form dynamics, and convergence to a deterministic limiting kernel under sequential width limits and Gaussian initialization; it also reviews tensor-program extensions to recurrent, residual, and transformer-like architectures.

key_findings.claim: Finite width and standard parameterization restore kernel evolution and therefore expose the boundary between lazy training and learned features.
key_findings.evidence: Higher-order kernels describe finite-width corrections, while the normalized NTK in standard parameterization can evolve during training; the survey connects depth-width scaling, ordered/chaotic phases, and feature-learning regimes that a frozen NTK cannot express.

key_findings.claim: NTKs support useful small-data and diagnostic applications but exact computation is prohibitive at modern visual scale.
key_findings.evidence: Reviewed applications include small-data convolutional kernels, condition-number NAS proxies, matrix completion, federated approximations, and spectral-bias analysis; a reported GTX-1080Ti extrapolation estimates roughly 160 years for Myrtle and 20,000 years for a modified ResNet-50 on ImageNet-scale kernel computation.

method.core_idea: Organize the NTK literature around parameter-gradient kernels, infinite-width limits, finite-width dynamics, applications, and practical limitations.
method.mechanism: The survey develops the empirical NTK as an inner product of Jacobian features, follows its deterministic infinite-width recursion and kernel-regression dynamics, then contrasts those results with higher-order, finite-width, and standard-parameterization analyses.
assumptions: Infinite-width theorems often take widths to infinity sequentially under Gaussian initialization and an NTK-specific scaling.
A fixed empirical or analytic NTK is an informative approximation when parameter movement is sufficiently small.
Kernel-level agreement is not by itself evidence that learned-feature behavior of practical networks has been captured.

techniques.role: Turns gradient training into function-space kernel dynamics.
Computes deterministic layerwise NNGP and NTK limits.
Tracks departures from the frozen-kernel limit at finite width.
Explains differential learning rates, spectral bias, and conditioning diagnostics.

evaluations.setting: Small-data image classification reviewed across convolutional NTK studies
evaluations.result: Convolutional kernels can be competitive in very small-data regimes, including a cited advantage over a standard ResNet-34 at up to 640 CIFAR examples.

evaluations.setting: Architecture ranking via NTK condition number
evaluations.result: Conditioning is reviewed as a cheap zero-cost proxy, but sensitivity to parameterization and task limits universality.
Exact empirical kernels are orders of magnitude beyond practical training cost for realistic high-resolution architectures.

limitations: This is a broad synthesis rather than a new theorem, algorithm, or controlled benchmark suite.
Many strongest statements require infinite width, Gaussian initialization, special parameterization, and sometimes squared loss or gradient flow.
Exact empirical-kernel storage, evaluation, and inversion scale quadratically or cubically with dataset size and poorly with model and input dimensions.
Frozen kernels cannot represent representation learning central to transfer, pretraining, and many finite-network gains.
failure_modes: Treating NTK equivalence as an explanation of all practical deep learning erases feature learning and optimizer-dependent representation change.
Finite networks near depth-width critical regimes can have non-deterministic and rapidly evolving kernels.
Architecture rankings based on conditioning can reverse when parameterization, data, loss, or training recipe changes.
Analytic kernels are available only for restricted operations, while naive empirical evaluation becomes computationally infeasible.
reusable_insights: Always distinguish empirical NTK, limiting NTK, NNGP, and a network's learned representation.
Report width, depth, parameterization, and kernel drift when using an NTK approximation.
Use kernel analyses as controlled baselines and diagnostics rather than automatically as mechanistic explanations.
Finite-width corrections and feature-learning limits provide the most productive interface between kernel theory and modern practice.
open_questions: Which computable kernel-drift statistics predict when finite networks leave the lazy regime?
Can scalable structured approximations retain useful empirical-NTK information at foundation-model scale?
Which training benefits require feature learning and which are already captured by initialization kernels?
How should NTK theory be extended to adaptive optimizers, nonstationary pretraining, and transfer?

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Jacot et al. introduce the limiting kernel and its constant-kernel training dynamics; this survey integrates that result with later theory, applications, and limitations.

competitive_landscape.title: Wide Neural Networks of Any Depth Evolve as Linear Models Under Gradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: Lee et al. establish first-order linearized dynamics and empirical agreement for wide networks; the survey situates linearization within the larger NTK literature.

competitive_landscape.title: Disentangling feature and lazy training in deep neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Geiger et al. experimentally and theoretically map the crossover between frozen-kernel lazy learning and feature learning, a core caveat synthesized by the survey.

competitive_landscape.title: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang and Hu construct infinite-width parameterizations that learn features and outperform NTK baselines on feature-dependent tasks, directly addressing a limitation of fixed NTKs.

competitive_landscape.title: Finite Depth and Width Corrections to the Neural Tangent Kernel
competitive_landscape.difference: Hanin and Nica quantify depth-width-dependent NTK fluctuations and first-update evolution rather than surveying the entire field.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: the paper's novelty is curatorial and pedagogical, not a new NTK result. Its value is an unusually broad bridge from formal infinite-width derivations through finite-width corrections and diverse applications to explicit computational and feature-learning limits.
reviewer_notes: All 47 extracted pages were reviewed, including definitions, limit theorems, finite-width sections, application chapters, comparison to standard parameterization and NNGP, and the limitations discussion. Primary competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23. Numerical runtime estimates are the survey's hardware-specific extrapolations, not reproduced measurements here.
